name: University of Florida Bat Houses
area: UF campus, Museum Road across from Lake Alice, Gainesville, Alachua County
coordinateNote: Entrance or parking coordinates from the November 12, 2026 gap review.
navigationDestination: UF Bat Houses, Museum Road (across from Lake Alice), Gainesville, FL
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Get there before sunset, sit on the benches along the Museum Road fence line or across by Lake Alice, and watch the western sky as the bats stream out 15-20 minutes after sunset. Bats may swoop close to catch insects.
cost: Free; free parking lot next to the field
access: Open field on campus, any evening, seven days a week; no staff on site. Follow posted campus parking signs.

conditions.summary: Viewing is open, but UF says bats emerge on calm evenings above 65 F; cold, wind or rain keeps them in. Late-November evenings are often cooler, so emergence is hit or miss. Colony numbers fell after the 2024 hurricanes (WUSF, Dec 2024); current count not verified. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

name: Juniper Springs Campground
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationDestination: Juniper Springs Recreation Area, 26701 FL-40, Silver Springs, FL 34488
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Seventy-six shaded sites in three loops under live oaks and palms, a short walk from the spring pool and the Juniper Run canoe launch. No hookups; hot showers and flush toilets. The gate is locked from 6 p.m. to 8 a.m. October to March.
access: Book and pay ahead. Stay limit: 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period Ocala WMA general gun season is Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027 in the Pipeline, Hopkins Prairie and Lake Delancy units (Church Lake Unit on the far west edge: Nov 14-22 and Nov 28 - Dec 6). FWC 2026-27 brochure: 'During the general gun season, camping is prohibited, except in designated campgrounds and Juniper Prairie Wilderness.' Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' This is a designated campground, so it stays legal for the whole trip. Hunters will be on the surrounding forest roads; deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange, and it is sensible to wear orange on trails outside the campground.

conditions.summary: Availability changes. Compare the saved individual site and night below, then confirm with the operator.

camp.sedanNote: Entrance and campground loops are paved (bituminous surface, maintenance level 5) in Forest Service road data, directly off SR 40.
camp.carSleepingNote: The provider’s parking and equipment fields do not confirm sleeping in an ordinary car. Ask the operator about your exact site.
camp.huntingNote: Ocala WMA general gun season is Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027 in the Pipeline, Hopkins Prairie and Lake Delancy units (Church Lake Unit on the far west edge: Nov 14-22 and Nov 28 - Dec 6). FWC 2026-27 brochure: 'During the general gun season, camping is prohibited, except in designated campgrounds and Juniper Prairie Wilderness.' Forest Service: 'Camping is allowed only in designated campsites during general gun season.' This is a designated campground, so it stays legal for the whole trip. Hunters will be on the surrounding forest roads; deer hunters must wear 500 sq in of fluorescent orange, and it is sensible to wear orange on trails outside the campground.
camp.gateHours: Campground gate is closed and locked from 8 p.m. to 8 a.m (March - Oct) and 6 p.m. to 8 a.m. (Oct - March). Campers who check-in after the gatehouse is closed must visit the Gatehouse the next morning to complete their check-in to their site. Failure to do so will lead to a 'no show' charge to your reservation and potential forfeiture of site.
camp.directions: From I-75, take Highway 40 east through Ocala and Silver Springs for approximately 36 miles to the Juniper Springs Recreation Area. From I-95, take the Ocala/Silver Springs Exit (Highway 40) west for approximately 37 miles to the Juniper Springs Recreation Area. From the intersection of Highway 40 and Highway 19, the campground is 4.5 miles west on Highway 40. The entrance is on the north side of Highway 40.
